title: Goal code as functional coordinate for one shared NCA local rule
hypothesis: A shared local transition rule conditioned on a 2D goal coordinate reaches unseen goal cells more reliably and with lower complete bytes than an independent per-goal rule bank.
physical_object: one shared local cell transition policy
mirror_coordinate: goal position (x,y), broadcast as a low-description code to the shared rule
logical_multiplicity: 25 global target behaviors from one local update function
controls: independent per-goal policies trained on seen goals
shared hard-tied rule without goal code

development.selection_metric: unseen-goal rollout success, mean steps, complete serialized bytes and active MACs

fresh.reason: single scoped NCA-inspired mechanism screen; no audit opened after native coordinate alias

paid_objects: goal coordinate codes or one-hot embeddings

compute.training_updates: shared rules 900; each observed independent goal rule 400

success_gate: At least 90% unseen-goal rollout success, >=25% fewer complete bytes than the independent rule bank, and strict improvement over the native coordinate-conditioned rule at matched compute.
failure_gate: Unseen-goal rollout failure, byte/compute gate miss, or exact native coordinate-code function/payload alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific value.
boundaries: Single-agent grid navigation using an NCA-inspired shared cell transition rule; no multi-cell pattern growth/regeneration claim.
No obstacles, continuous dynamics, learned morphology or biological realism.
No learned neural cellular automaton benchmark or accelerator runtime claim.
